rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps
rows.expected_answer: You choose the order and the best answer is 6. Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer:
You choose the order. Timestamps don't matter here. With X=2, apply **Hardened Scales** first and then **Doubling Season**: (2+1)×2 = **6** counters. The other order gives 2×2+1 = **5**.

**Walking Ballista**'s "This creature enters with X +1/+1 counters on it" is a replacement effect (614.1c), and both of your enchantments also modify that event. Doubling Season's ruling confirms it "affects permanents that enter with counters," and Hardened Scales has a matching ruling.

Per 616.1, when two or more replacement effects try to modify the same event, the affected object's controller picks which one applies first. Neither of these is a self-replacement effect and neither is a control or copy effect, so 616.1e lets you choose either one. After that, per 616.1f, the process repeats with the effect that's still left.

The Hardened Scales ruling says the same thing: "you choose the order to apply those effects." So you'd normally go Scales, then Season, and get a 6/6 Ballista.

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer:
No. Under **Blood Moon**, each Tron land just taps for {R}. Your three lands make 3 red mana, not 7 colorless, and **Urza's Tower** can't make {C}{C}{C}.

Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." That is a type-changing effect, applied in layer 4 (`613.1d`). Per `305.7`, when an effect sets a land's subtype to a basic land type, the land "loses all abilities generated from its rules text, its old land types" and gains the mana ability for its new type. So the Tower loses its whole "{T}: Add {C}. If you control an Urza's Mine and an Urza's Power-Plant, add {C}{C}{C} instead." ability. Only "{T}: Add {R}" is left. The bonus looks for land types, not names, and your other lands no longer have the Urza's Mine or Urza's Power-Plant subtype. They're just Mountains now. Blood Moon doesn't change names or supertypes, so the lands are still called Urza's Tower and so on, and they're still nonbasic. That's why Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

The Scryfall ruling on Urborg confirms this: when a Moon effect sets it to a basic land type, "it won't turn lands into Swamps, no matter in what order those effects started to apply."

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is just a regular **Tarmogoyf**. It doesn't get your +1/+1 counters or the **Giant Growth** bonus, but it does copy the Goyf's ability that sets its size, so it is always exactly as big as an unpumped Goyf.

Per `707.2`, a copy takes only the copiable values, meaning the printed text as changed by other copy effects. "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." Your two counters and Giant Growth's "+3/+3 until end of turn" stay with your Goyf. The Clone ruling says the same: it doesn't copy "whether it has any counters on it" or "any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness".

On the */*+1 part: the Goyf's power and toughness come from its rules text, and per `707.2a` a copy "acquires the abilities of the object it's copying because those values are derived from its rules text." So the Clone has "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1", referring to itself. It keeps counting the graveyards on its own, just like your Goyf.

For example, with 4 card types in graveyards, the Clone is 4/5. Your Goyf is 4/5 + 2 counters + 3/3 = 9/10 this turn.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
Your regular creatures stay 1/1 with no abilities either way. Only the enchantments change, and the result depends on timestamps.

**Humility out first, Opalescence later (your case):**
- **Opalescence** is not a creature. It affects only "Each other non-Aura enchantment", so it doesn't animate itself.
- **Humility** becomes a 4/4 enchantment creature with no abilities.
- Your other creatures are 1/1 with no abilities. Opalescence doesn't touch non-enchantments.

Here's how the layers work it out:
- Layer 4: Opalescence makes Humility a creature.
- Layer 6: Humility's effect removes all creature abilities, including Humility's own. Its effect still finishes applying anyway, because per `613.6` an effect that has started to apply "will continue to be applied to the same set of objects in each other applicable layer" even if the ability is removed partway through.
- Layer 7b: Both effects set base P/T, so they apply in timestamp order (`613.4b`, `613.7`). Humility's is earlier, so it makes Humility 1/1 first. Opalescence's later effect then sets it to its mana value, 4/4.

**Opalescence out first, Humility later:** Layers 4 and 6 work out the same. In 7b, Opalescence's effect applies first and Humility's later effect overrides it. So Humility is a 1/1 with no abilities, like every other creature. Opalescence is still not a creature.

The Scryfall ruling on both cards walks through exactly these two orders: Opalescence first gives 4/4 then 1/1; Humility first gives 1/1 then 4/4.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes. **Valki, God of Lies** is a modal double-faced card, so you can cast it as **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** for {5}{B}{R}. Per `712.11b` you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and per `712.11c` only that face is checked to see whether it can be cast.

No, it isn't a planeswalker card in your hand, library or graveyard. Per `712.8a`, outside the battlefield and stack it "has only the characteristics of its front face", so there it's only Valki, a creature card. On the battlefield it has only the characteristics of the face that's up (`712.8f`).

That matters less than you might think, because **Vraska's Contempt** and **Kaya's Ghostform** only look at permanents on the battlefield. Tibalt on the battlefield is a planeswalker, so Contempt can target it and Ghostform can enchant it.

One catch with Ghostform: "return that card to the battlefield" brings the card back from the graveyard or exile, not from the stack. Per `712.14` it enters front face up, so you get Valki back, not Tibalt.

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?

Nicol Bolas, the Ravager (UBR) is legal because every color in its identity is in Kenrith's (903.5c). 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. **1)** Color identity counts the mana symbols in a card's mana cost *and* its rules text (903.4). Kenrith costs {4}{W}, and his abilities include "{R}: All creatures gain trample and haste", "{1}{G}: Put a +1/+1 counter", "{3}{U}: Target player draws a card" and "{4}{B}: Put target creature card from a graveyard onto the battlefield". That makes his color identity all five colors. Bolas's identity is blue, black and red. Its back face also counts (903.4d), and it adds nothing outside those three colors. Graveyard and exile work differently: there it's a state-based action that lets you move him afterward (903.9a).

rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose. Damage from the Clone doesn't count toward Rafiq's 21, and damage from Fling never counts, because it isn't combat damage.

**Clone isn't a commander.** Being a commander "is not a characteristic of the object represented by the card; rather, it is an attribute of the card itself" (`903.3`). A copy of a commander doesn't get that status. The example under `903.3` says outright that "A permanent that’s copying a commander ... is not a commander." So the 6 damage from the Clone is ordinary combat damage. Your total of commander damage from Rafiq stays at 15.

**21 means combat damage from the same commander.** Per `903.10a`, "A player who’s been dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander over the course of the game loses the game." Fling isn't combat damage, so it never adds to that total. That holds even if she sacrifices the real Rafiq to it. It's also Fling dealing the damage, not the commander. It still takes life off you as normal (`119.2`), so it can kill you by bringing your life to 0 (`119.6`).

One more thing: Rafiq gives a creature that attacks alone exalted (+1/+1) and double strike. If the real Rafiq attacks alone with 15 already on you, 6 more combat damage from it would put you at 21.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
